solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Before start of fight heavyweight backed Prince a lot

indicators.note: something backed is moved in the rear direction, so the word for heavyweight is read from its end

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight
Prince Hal, Shakespeare's young Henry V

indicators.note: the start of a word is just its opening letter, so only that one is taken from fight

parts.note: first letter of fight

explanation.surface: A boxing build-up: before the bout, the heavyweight backed a prince heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' places the prince ahead of the letter from fight; the reversed heavyweight comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Not half is British slang meaning very much or extremely, as in 'did he complain? Not half!'

clue.text: New American perfume being developed

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
A is the abbreviation for American
scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: A new US fragrance is in development.
explanation.walkthrough: New looks like part of the definition but supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into existence and beginning to grow or form.

clue.text: I left upset ram without something it would eat?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the ram word sits round the other pair

parts.note: a tup is a ram

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the pair is read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone has left a ram agitated by depriving it of food.
explanation.walkthrough: The it of the definition is the ram, which would happily munch a garden flower; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip is a spring bulb flower, the sort of garden plant a grazing sheep would gladly eat.

clue.text: Are big cats unable to head off insects?

indicators.note: with the head taken off, the first letter of the word for unable is dropped

parts.note: can't means unable
lions are big cats

explanation.surface: A question about whether lions and tigers cannot head off some threat.
explanation.walkthrough: Head off sounds like intercepting something; it means beheading a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Antlions are insects whose larvae dig pits in sand to trap ants.

clue.text: Repulse thin metal sword

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to thwart or beat back
second meaning: metal beaten into a very thin sheet
third meaning: a light blunted fencing blade

explanation.surface: Fend off an attacker with a slender metal blade.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Foil means to frustrate an attack, a sheet of beaten metal, and a fencing weapon.

clue.text: Crushes relative

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split as two words: treads on, squashes underfoot
second meaning: a family member by marriage

explanation.walkthrough: Read as STEPS ON the first part is a phrasal verb meaning crushes; read whole it is a family relation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is the son of one's spouse from an earlier partnership, a relation acquired by marriage.

clue.text: Loud senator going around with tin

indicators.note: going around suggests the letters are spun about and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy politician making the rounds with a collecting tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentorian means extremely powerful in voice, after Stentor, the loud-voiced herald in Homer.

clue.text: Hospital department about to finally serve main course

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the next word, serve

parts.note: last letter of serve

explanation.surface: A hospital kitchen at last gets round to dishing up dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: In North America the entrée is the main dish; in Britain it can be a course before the main.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrée is used, especially in America, for the principal dish of a meal.

clue.text: Chef's aid holding 8?

parts.note: a holding of shares is stock
the number eight is a cube, two times two times two

explanation.surface: A cook's helper keeps hold of the answer to 8 down.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 looks like a cross-reference to 8 down; it is the plain number, a perfect cube, and the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock cube is a compressed block of dried broth that cooks dissolve to make stock quickly.

clue.text: Country song, say, in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means running backwards, so the whole string of pieces is read from the end

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
eg, for example, means say
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country music track played backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Country song sounds like country and western music; country is the definition and song a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a nation in West Africa, the continent's most populous.

clue.text: Diamond is an American singer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single gem set on its own in a ring
second meaning: a songbird of the thrush family found in the Americas

explanation.surface: Neil Diamond introduced as a US pop vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital D suggests the singer Neil Diamond, but the singer here is a bird and the diamond a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitaire is a gem mounted alone, and also the name of New World thrushes noted for their song.

clue.text: Host runs out in skimpy underwear

indicators.note: out means removed, so the runs abbreviation is taken away from the word for host

parts.note: a host is a great crowd
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A party host runs outside wearing very little.
explanation.walkthrough: Host means a crowd here, not the person giving a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a minimal piece of underwear with a narrow strip at the back.

clue.text: Unorthodox priest's wittiness

indicators.note: unorthodox means departing from the established order, so the letters leave their usual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleric with heterodox views is admired for his quick humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is a French borrowing for lively wit and sparkle in conversation.

clue.text: Uncovered runner disturbing course of events

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person dashing about naked in public

definitions.note: describes the person, one who disrupts proceedings
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who disrupts the events held on a racecourse or sports ground

explanation.surface: A rug-less racehorse upsets how the day unfolds.
explanation.walkthrough: Course of events sounds like the way things happen, but it is the racecourse or ground where events take place.
explanation.definitionFit: This is someone who runs naked through a public place, typically invading a sports field mid-match.

clue.text: Fragrance puddings possess?

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert
to possess is to have

explanation.surface: A whimsical query whether desserts own a perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: Afters is an informal British word for pudding, the course after the main one.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a scented lotion men apply after shaving, so it is a fragrance.

clue.text: A natural player might be using it

definitions.text: A natural player might be using it

parts.words: A natural player might be using it
parts.note: surface reading: a gifted performer, a natural, employing some tool; setter's reading: the note A natural, which a musician pitches against a pronged steel device

explanation.walkthrough: A natural looks like a person with innate talent; in music it is the note A, neither sharp nor flat, the standard tuning pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-pronged instrument vibrates at a fixed pitch, commonly the note A, so musicians use it to tune.

clue.text: Shop with mint and herb books

parts.note: mint condition means brand new
sage is a herb
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A store stocking mint, herbs and books.
explanation.walkthrough: Mint looks like another herb beside herb, but it means brand new.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent is a British shop selling newspapers, magazines, sweets and tobacco.

clue.text: Copper with degree on an island

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A police officer with a university qualification posted to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but it is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean, lying south of Florida.

clue.text: Shout about garden around conservatory

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the garden word wraps the jumbled letters

parts.note: to hoe is to garden, weeding with a tool

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone yells about the garden surrounding a glasshouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Garden is a verb here, and the tool word splits after its second letter to take the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothouse is a heated glass building for plants, much like a conservatory.

clue.text: Hood caught wolf endlessly in disguise

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without an end means the final letter of wolf is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A villain in a hood is captured: a wolf in disguise, like the one in Red Riding Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a loose hood, especially one worn by a monk.

clue.text: Indian drink in Cricket Club — Derby, say

indicators.note: in places the drink inside the club abbreviation

parts.note: CC is the standard abbreviation for Cricket Club
lassi is a yoghurt drink from India

explanation.surface: A cricket club in Derby serves an Indian drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the Midlands town with its county cricket club; it is the Derby, a famous English horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is one of the five Classics, the major English flat races for three-year-old horses.

clue.text: China backed educational reformist going round about quickly!

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so the reformist's name encloses the other piece

parts.note: Michael Gove, the UK education secretary who pushed through school reforms

indicators.note: backed means sent rearwards, so the word for china is read from its last letter

parts.note: rhyming slang: china plate means mate
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A friend supports a school reformer who is dashing about at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang for a friend. Michael Gove was the British minister in charge of schools in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Get a move on is an urgent instruction to hurry up, an exclamation meaning go faster.

clue.text: Ordinary person regarded as certain to qualify

definitions.text: person regarded as certain to qualify

explanation.surface: An everyday person thought to be a sure thing for selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means normal or unaffected, and as a noun someone so gifted they are a sure choice.

clue.text: Shadow one going in part of Italy

indicators.note: going in means entering, so the numeral is inserted into the shadow word

parts.note: an umbra is the darkest part of a shadow
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone's shadow entering a region of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a landlocked region of central Italy, home to Perugia and Assisi.

clue.text: Scaremonger gets top celebs to carry weapon

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside, so the celebs phrase wraps round the weapon

parts.note: the A-list is the top tier of celebrities
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A fearmonger persuades leading stars to bear arms.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist is someone who spreads needless fear, exactly what a scaremonger does.

clue.text: Warning doctor about onset of hepatitis

indicators.note: about means around, so the doctoring verb is placed round the selected letter

parts.note: to doctor a patient is to treat them

indicators.note: the onset is the very beginning, so only the opening letter of hepatitis is used

parts.note: first letter of hepatitis

explanation.surface: A physician warns of a patient showing early signs of liver disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor is a verb here, not the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat can be a warning of something bad to come, as in the threat of rain.

clue.text: Minor player added

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a film or stage walk-on with no lines
second meaning: additional, more than usual

explanation.surface: A junior team member brought in as a late addition.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a background actor in a crowd scene, and as an adjective it means additional.

clue.text: Part of Noddy's haircut

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pouch in a bird's gullet, here of the noddy, a tropical tern
second meaning: a very short hairstyle

explanation.surface: A detail of the hairstyle of Noddy, the children's toy character.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital N suggests Enid Blyton's Noddy; a noddy is also a seabird, and a crop is part of a bird's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is the food-storage pouch in a bird's throat, and also a closely cut hairstyle.

clue.text: Completely avoid an unpleasant thing

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to swerve away, used with off or away, from something disagreeable

explanation.surface: Advice to steer entirely clear of anything nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer as an adverb means perpendicularly or completely; as a verb, sheer off means turn aside to avoid something unwelcome.

clue.text: Play it like Hendrix — no strings attached!

definitions.meaning: setter's reading: mime a rock guitarist's playing on an imaginary instrument that literally has no strings
surface reading: the idiom for a deal with no conditions

explanation.walkthrough: Jimi Hendrix was a celebrated rock guitarist; the idiom about conditions turns literal, since the instrument here does not exist.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the mimed playing of an imaginary electric instrument, copying a rock star's moves without anything in hand.

clue.text: Excessive silver in church dwelling

indicators.note: in places the excessive and silver pieces inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OTT stands for over the top
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Too much silverware on display in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, typically in the countryside, so it is a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Bucket clergyman put in Triumph

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so the clergyman goes inside the bucket word

parts.note: a pail is a bucket
Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar is stuffed into a bucket inside a Triumph car.
explanation.walkthrough: Triumph, capitalised as the car make, is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win or come out on top, a synonym of the verb triumph.
